paragraphs.text: What is headless WordPress? It is a setup where WordPress manages content only, and a separate front end displays it. In a normal WordPress site, the same system stores content and builds every page with a theme. In a decoupled WordPress site, the theme is removed and a modern framework fetches content through an API, then builds fast pages from it.

WordPress powers more than 43% of all websites, so many teams already know how to use it. Headless WordPress development keeps that familiar editor and removes the parts that often slow sites down, such as heavy themes and page-builder plugins on the public site.

paragraphs.html: Headless vs traditional WordPress comes down to speed, security and flexibility against simplicity. Traditional WordPress is quicker to set up and works with thousands of themes and plugins out of the box. A headless WordPress website loads faster, exposes less of WordPress to attackers, and lets one content source feed a website, an app and other channels.

paragraphs.text: The trade-off is that some plugins that change the front end will not work headless, and design changes need a developer. When should you go headless? Usually when speed, security or multi-channel publishing matter more than plugin convenience.

sections.h2: What Headless WordPress Services Does Teknoppy Offer?

items.title: WordPress With Next JS
items.text: WordPress with Next JS is our most common setup. Next.js builds pages on the server or in advance, so visitors and search engines receive complete HTML immediately. Pages update automatically when editors publish changes in WordPress.

items.title: WPGraphQL Development
items.html:
WPGraphQL development adds a GraphQL API to WordPress through a free, widely used plugin. The front end asks for exactly the content each page needs in one request, which keeps pages fast and code simple. It also makes adding new content types later much easier.

WPGraphQL vs REST API: WordPress also includes a built-in REST API. REST is fine for simple sites, while WPGraphQL is usually cleaner for complex pages that combine posts, custom fields, menus and related content. We choose during discovery based on your content.

items.title: ACF Headless Setup
items.text: ACF headless setup structures your content with Advanced Custom Fields, so editors fill in clear fields such as headline, summary, image and call to action, instead of designing pages by hand. Content stays consistent, and the front end decides how it looks.

items.title: Headless WordPress Preview Setup
items.text: Editors want to see changes before publishing. Our headless WordPress preview setup lets them click Preview in WordPress and see the draft exactly as it will appear on the live front end.

items.title: Headless WordPress Multilingual Site
items.text: A headless WordPress multilingual site serves English, Arabic, Malayalam or other languages from one WordPress install, with separate URLs, hreflang tags and right-to-left layouts where needed.

sections.h2: Headless WordPress Sites We Commonly Build

paragraphs.text: Typical projects include news and magazine sites that publish many articles a day, corporate sites for companies with several brands, tourism and hospitality sites with heavy image galleries, and knowledge hubs for training institutes. Most already run on WordPress, have years of content worth keeping, and have outgrown a slow theme.

sections.h2: Can Editors Still Use the WordPress Dashboard?

paragraphs.text: Can editors still use the WordPress dashboard? Yes. Your team logs in to WordPress, writes posts, uploads images and manages pages exactly as before. Only the public website changes. Most editors notice one difference: the site they publish to is noticeably faster.
We train your editors after launch and provide a short guide covering previews, custom fields and publishing.

Headless WordPress hosting has two parts. WordPress runs on a small, private server that only your team and the front end can reach. The front end runs on a fast global network, such as Vercel or a managed cloud platform, and serves pages to visitors.

Headless WordPress security improves because the WordPress login and admin are no longer on the public website. We also limit API access, keep plugins to a minimum, enforce strong passwords and two-step login, and apply WordPress updates on a fixed schedule.

sections.h2: Is Headless WordPress Good for SEO?

paragraphs.text: Is headless WordPress good for SEO? Yes, when the front end renders full HTML on the server, which is how we build it. Pages load faster, metadata comes directly from WordPress fields, and sitemaps, redirects and structured data are generated automatically. Content stays readable for Google and for AI search tools. Your existing URLs can also be kept, so rankings earned by older posts carry over to the new front end without a reset.

sections.h2: How Much Does Headless WordPress Cost?

paragraphs.text: How much does headless WordPress cost? A headless build costs more than a theme-based WordPress site, because the front end is custom-built. The difference is usually recovered through faster pages, lower security risk and fewer plugin problems over the following years.
Every project is quoted after discovery, and the quote is fixed for the agreed scope. Each quote for headless WordPress development lists exactly what is included, including hosting recommendations.

items.q: How long does headless WordPress development take?
items.a: A company website usually takes 6 to 8 weeks of headless WordPress development. A large or multilingual site takes 10 to 12 weeks. We confirm the timeline in writing after discovery.

items.q: Can my existing WordPress site go headless?
items.a: Yes. In most cases your posts, pages, media and users stay in the same WordPress install. We add an API, restructure content fields where needed and build the new front end alongside the old site, so you switch over only when everything is tested.

Plugins that manage content, such as custom fields, SEO fields and translation, usually keep working. Plugins that change the front-end design do not, because the theme is replaced. We review every plugin during discovery and suggest alternatives where needed.
